Subject: Priv infra CI ownership + deploy simulation results and rollback playbook

Hi Joe / Acme devs —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached are the outputs from the dry-run we ran against your staging VPC (priv-deploy-sim-results.csv) plus an initial rollback playbook (rollback-playbook-v1.pdf). High level asks for this thread:

1) Review the simulation CSV and confirm the two egress failures we flagged (lines 23, 47) are expected behavior for your transit ACLs.
2) Confirm CI ownership for the Terraform modules vs Helm values for the enclave stack. We proposed: Acme owns zone-level network TF modules; Redwood owns kube/helm configs for model-serving.
3) Sign off on the proposed rollback criteria (attached) or provide concrete edits.

Quick notes on the simulation: we executed a staged deploy that creates a new privstack environment, applies terraform modules, runs k8s helm chart deploys, then performs traffic-shaping tests and an egress validation suite. The CSV attaches per-step latencies and an indicator column (PASS/FAIL). The plan also includes the terraform plan patch (terraform-plan.patch) with the resource address changes we would apply in a canary.

Please reply with: a) who will own the TF module PR approvals, b) whether we should run the next simulation with stricter egress rules (we can run that tomorrow morning PST), and c) any immediate redlines to the rollback playbook.

Thanks — aiming to freeze the rollout plan by EOD Friday so we can schedule the canary deploy next week.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security (Priv Deploy)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: priv-deploy-sim-results.csv (csv text), rollback-playbook-v1.pdf (pdf stub), terraform-plan.patch (patch text)
From: Joe Tucker <joe.tucker@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-corp-dev@acme.com, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI ownership + deploy simulation results and rollback playbook

Kimberly —

Thanks for the detailed packet. Quick responses inline: 

On the egress failures you called out: our infra team thinks line 23 corresponds to a new monitoring agent outbound to an external metrics provider (we intentionally block that until we onboard them). Line 47 looks like a NAT gateway exhaustion simulation — that one is concerning. Can you confirm which step consumed the most concurrent connections in your traffic sim?

Ownership: Acme can take zone-level TF PR approvals but we need Redwood to lead the canary Helm roll (you have the runtime knobs). Proposed split looks fine otherwise.

Rollback playbook: high-level looks good, but request that we add an explicit step to revoke ephemeral keys created during the canary and a short section on evidence capture for our SOC audit (timestamps + terraform state snapshots).

We can do a tighter egress run tomorrow 09/11 10:00am ET (07:00 PT). Vivek / Marissa, is that window OK?

Joe
Senior Cloud Engineer — Acme Financial
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Joe Tucker <joe.tucker@acme.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI ownership + deploy simulation results and rollback playbook

Joe / team —

Thanks, Joe — good catch on the NAT exhaustion. From our sim logs the spike correlates with the service-discovery probe step (step 6) where we spawn 120 short-lived connections to validate endpoint convergence. I clipped the relevant lines into terraform-plan.patch and added an option to limit discovery probe concurrency:

--- a/modules/discovery/main.tf
+++ b/modules/discovery/main.tf
@@
- resource "null_resource" "probe" {
-   count = var.probe_count
+ resource "null_resource" "probe" {
+   count = min(var.probe_count, var.max_concurrency)

The suggested default for var.max_concurrency is 30 which eliminates the NAT burst in our test. We also added a quick k8s readiness probe backoff in the Helm values to space pod startups (see patch).

On your ask to capture terraform state snapshots: agreed — we will add a post-apply hook in CI to copy the statefile to the evidence bucket with a timestamped key and restrict read access to the audit role. I'll add the hook as a dry-run stage first.

Availability: 09/11 07:00 PT works for our infra automation runner. We'll run the tighter egress test then and share results (~90m run).

—Vivek
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Joe / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary / decisions from our side after reviewing Vivek's patch and the tightening run: 

- Concurrency limit: set var.max_concurrency=30 in discovery module (Agreed). Vivek will open a PR with the patch and mark it as a non-disruptive config guard. (Owner: Vivek; target merge: 2026-09-14)
- Canary ownership: Redwood to execute Helm canary roll and smoke tests; Acme to review and approve Terraform module PRs for zone/network changes. (Owners: Redwood/Acme; target: canary week of 2026-09-20)
- Evidence capture: add CI post-apply stage to copy terraform state + plan artifacts to audit bucket; include a retained 90-day snapshot for SOC. (Owner: Marissa; target: 2026-09-16)
- Rollback playbook edits: Acme requested ephemeral key revocation and timestamped evidence section. We've accepted both edits; updated PDF attached. (Attachment: rollback-playbook-v1.pdf)

Next steps: Vivek will open two PRs (terraform discovery concurrency + helm startup backoff). Marissa will add the CI post-apply hook in a feature branch and run smoke tests in the sandbox. Joe, please assign a reviewer from Acme for the TF PRs once Vivek has them up.

If there are no objections we'll lock the schedule by EOD Monday and run the canary on 2026-09-21 (non-business hours window).

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security (Priv Deploy)
Redwood Inference
